meta.title: SkiPick — Compare Japan Ski Resorts
meta.description: Browse Tokyo-area ski resorts on a map and compare prices, runs, and travel time side by side.

footer.note: SkiPick · Data maintained by the community and official sources

home.subtitle:
Stop cross-checking five different sites. 
Resort areas are outlined right on the map — pick one and compare price, runs, and travel time at a glance.
home.feature1Desc: Resort boundaries are overlaid on a real terrain map, so location, size, and nearby resorts are obvious at a glance — not just a lone pin.
home.feature2Desc: Pick 2–4 resorts and see price, run mix, lift count, and travel time laid out together — like comparing flights.
home.feature3Desc: Gondola status, today's snow conditions — the details official sites never update, added by whoever's actually on the mountain.
home.newsIntro: Website updates, release notes, and feature changes.

news.pageSubtitle: Latest updates, website changes, and release notes.

2026-08-06.title: Version 0.5 is Updated
2026-08-06.excerpt: SkiPick 0.5 is now live! Currently in testing, it only supports ski resorts near Tokyo.
2026-08-06.content:
This is a one-person project, so please be patient with the limited time available.
The current version only supports ski resorts near Tokyo. Data is based on official information for the 25-26 season, and 26-27 season data has not yet been updated.

Future development plans:
- Early-bird data for the 26-27 season
- Support for community feedback features
- Support for ski resorts nationwide

site-refresh-2026-08.title: Website refresh and new home experience
site-refresh-2026-08.excerpt: The homepage has been redesigned with a more visual resort overview and clearer comparison entry points.
site-refresh-2026-08.content: We refreshed the overall visual style of the site, strengthened the map-driven entry experience, and improved the hero section so new visitors can understand the product faster. The featured resort preview and the latest updates are now displayed more clearly on the homepage.

compare-flow-update.title: Comparison flow improved for quicker decisions
compare-flow-update.excerpt: The compare experience now highlights the most useful metrics first, making side-by-side decisions faster.
compare-flow-update.content: We reorganized the compare screen so travel time, price, and run mix are easier to scan. This makes it simpler to shortlist resorts before you decide which one to visit.

map-guidance-update.title: Map guidance and resort detail improvements
map-guidance-update.excerpt: A clearer overview and better guidance were added to the resort map and detail pages.
map-guidance-update.content: We refined the map interaction flow and added more direct guidance on how to explore resort details. The result is a smoother experience for users who want to discover specific ski areas quickly.

map.title: Resort Map
map.subtitle: Click a shaded area on the map to see resort details.

echigo-yuzawa.title: Echigo-Yuzawa & Chuetsu
echigo-yuzawa.summary: Directly accessible by Shinkansen. Covering the heavy-snow Chuetsu area including Yuzawa, Uonuma, Tokamachi, and Tsunan. Home to top resorts like GALA Yuzawa, Naeba, Kandatsu, and Kagura.

gunma-tochigi.title: Gunma / Tochigi
gunma-tochigi.summary: Located in northern Gunma and Tochigi prefectures, easily reached by car or tour bus. Famous for high-quality natural powder snow and versatile terrains like Kawaba and Oze Iwakura.

joshinetsu.title: Joshinetsu Kogen
joshinetsu.summary: Spanning Nagano, Gunma, and Niigata prefectures. Highly accessible via Shinkansen with early-season operations (e.g. Karuizawa Prince Resort). Features luxury outlet shopping and top resort hotels.

shiga-nozawa.title: Shiga & Nozawa
shiga-nozawa.summary: Home to Japan's largest unified ski resort Shiga Kogen, historic Nozawa Onsen, tree-run powder haven Madarao, and Ryuo SORA Terrace — the pinnacle of Nagano powder & hot springs.

hakuba.title: Hakuba Valley
hakuba.summary: World-renowned international winter destination in the Japanese Alps. Featuring legendary resorts like Happo-one, Tsugaike, Goryu, and Hakuba47 with world-class powder snow and vast terrain.

compare.subtitle: Select up to {max} resorts to compare side by side. Departure point is fixed to Tokyo Station.

gala-yuzawa.name: GALA Yuzawa
gala-yuzawa.summary: Connected directly to the shinkansen station, so there's almost no transfer time — the classic Tokyo day-trip pick.

naeba.name: Naeba
naeba.summary: A large resort linked by gondola to the Kagura area, good for skiers who want a mix of terrain.

kagura.name: Kagura
kagura.summary: Known for its powder and natural terrain, with the Tashiro, Kagura, and Mitsumata areas connected. Long season.

kawaba.name: Kawaba
kawaba.summary: No direct shinkansen, but an easy exit off the Kan-etsu Expressway — a favorite among drivers.

oze-iwakura.name: Oze Iwakura
oze-iwakura.summary: A 120-person gondola and excellent summit views make this a popular pick with families.

karuizawa-prince.name: Karuizawa Prince
karuizawa-prince.summary: Gentle slopes with a small vertical drop, paired with the outlet mall next door — a top choice for beginners and families.

kandatsu.name: Kandatsu Snow Resort
kandatsu.summary: Famous for all-night skiing and terrain parks, close to Yuzawa station and popular with younger skiers and snowboarders.

iwappara.name: Iwappara
iwappara.summary: Features a famous ultra-wide single-slope run with gentle gradient, ideal for beginners and family practice.

yuzawa-park.name: Yuzawa Park
yuzawa-park.summary: A hotel-ski slopes direct resort. Compact and sheltered from wind, great for kids and relaxed practice.

yuzawa-nakazato.name: Yuzawa Nakazato
yuzawa-nakazato.summary: Directly connected to JR Echigo-Nakazato Station, featuring train carriage rest areas and a fun kids park.

yuzawa-kogen.name: Yuzawa Kogen
yuzawa-kogen.summary: Access the summit via one of the world's largest 166-person ropeways. Summit links to GALA while base offers gentle slopes.

naspa-ski-garden.name: NASPA Ski Garden
naspa-ski-garden.summary: A rare skiers-only resort (no snowboards allowed) with immaculately groomed runs for peaceful skiing.

ishiuchi-maruyama.name: Ishiuchi Maruyama
ishiuchi-maruyama.summary: A classic historic resort equipped with modern hybrid lifts (Sunrise Express) and outstanding night skiing.

maiko.name: Maiko Snow Resort
maiko.summary: Just 1 minute off the Shiozawa-Ishiuchi IC. Spans 3 areas with a maximum run length of 6,000 meters.

joetsu-kokusai.name: Joetsu Kokusai
joetsu-kokusai.summary: A massive mega-resort with 4 main zones and the iconic Green Plaza Hotel right at the foot of the slopes.

hakkaisan.name: Muikamachi Hakkaisan
hakkaisan.summary: 800m vertical drop, steep inclines, and deep un-groomed powder fields make this a haven for experts.

hakkaisan-sanroku.name: Hakkaisan Sanroku Ski Resort
hakkaisan-sanroku.summary: A cozy family resort located at the foot of Mt. Hakkai with wide gentle slopes, perfect for children and beginners.

muika.name: Muika Snow Resort
muika.summary: Offers a main slope over 200m wide alongside un-groomed powder zones, overlooking the Hakkaisan peaks.

chateau-shiozawa.name: Chateau Shiozawa Ski Resort
chateau-shiozawa.summary: Adjacent to Maiko and Joetsu Kokusai. Features wide, gentle slopes and uncrowded atmosphere, perfect for beginners and family practice.

nakazato-snow-wood.name: Nakazato Snow Wood Ski Resort
nakazato-snow-wood.summary: Directly connected to Hotel Angel Grandia Echigo Nakazato. Gentle slopes and child-friendly design make it ideal for families with young children.

suhara.name: Suhara Ski Resort
suhara.summary: A traditional local resort in Uonuma city known for deep snow and great summit panoramas.

yakushi.name: Yakushi Ski Resort
yakushi.summary: A compact resort next to an Onsen town, featuring gentle slopes ideal for basic practice.

koide.name: Koide Ski Resort
koide.summary: Located close to the city center and train station, convenient for quick practice sessions.

okutadami-maruyama.name: Okutadami Maruyama Ski Resort
okutadami-maruyama.summary: A legendary spring skiing haven tucked in a deep snow sanctuary, operating well into May.

new-green-pia-tsunan.name: New Green Pia Tsunan Ski Resort
new-green-pia-tsunan.summary: A comprehensive hotel resort featuring diverse snow activities alongside enjoyable slopes.

kashimayari.name: Kashimayari Ski Resort
kashimayari.summary: Located at the southern end of Hakuba Valley overlooking Lake Nakatsuna with great family amenities.

jiigatake.name: Jiigatake Ski Resort
jiigatake.summary: Extremely safe and gentle beginner slopes with a fun kids snow park, perfect for young families.

tsugaike-kogen.name: Tsugaike Kogen Ski Resort
tsugaike-kogen.summary: Famous for the 1km wide gentle Kan-no-kane slope, plus heli-skiing and backcountry powder riding.

hakuba-iwatake.name: Hakuba Iwatake Snow Field
hakuba-iwatake.summary: Offers a 360-degree panoramic view of the Northern Alps, featuring the iconic Mountain Harbor deck.

hakuba-goryu-47.name: Hakuba Goryu & Hakuba47 Ski Resort
hakuba-goryu-47.summary: A combined giant resort connected at the summit under one shared lift pass, featuring night skiing, powder snow, and Hakuba's top terrain park.

hakuba-cortina.name: Hakuba Norikura Onsen & Hakuba Cortina
hakuba-cortina.summary: Interconnected ski area combining Hakuba Norikura Onsen and Hakuba Cortina under a shared lift pass, famous for deep powder snow and tree runs.

hakuba-sanosaka.name: Hakuba Sanosaka Ski Resort
hakuba-sanosaka.summary: Picturesque setting overlooking Lake Aoki, peaceful slopes, mogul courses, and terrain park.

hakuba-happo-one.name: Hakuba Happo-one Snow Resort
hakuba-happo-one.summary: Host of the 1998 Winter Olympics, boasting over 1,000m vertical drop, steep pitches, and long runs.

sugadaira-kogen.name: Sugadaira Kogen Snow Resort
sugadaira-kogen.summary: Located in one of Honshu's coldest plateaus, famous for diamond dust and fast, perfectly groomed hard-pack snow. Offers 60 courses across three peaks.

palcall-tsumagoi.name: Palcall Tsumagoi Resort
palcall-tsumagoi.summary: Home to Kanto's longest gondola (3,193m) with a summit elevation of 2,050m. Famous for 6:00 AM Sunrise Skiing on pristine morning groomers.

manza-onsen.name: Manza Onsen Ski Resort
manza-onsen.summary: Operated by Prince Hotels. Situated at over 1,800m elevation, offering exquisite powder snow paired with famous rich milky-white sulfur hot springs.

kusatsu-onsen.name: Kusatsu Onsen Ski Resort
kusatsu-onsen.summary: Located right next to Kusatsu Onsen town. Features modern Pulse Gondola and Tenguyama slopes, combining skiing with famous hot spring walks.

kazawa-snow-area.name: Kazawa Snow Area
kazawa-snow-area.summary: Renowned for its early season opening in late November and firm, high-quality groomed snow ideal for race training and early-season skiing.

minenohara-kogen.name: Minenohara Kogen Ski Resort (Ninja Snow Highland)
minenohara-kogen.summary: Cozy resort at 1,500m elevation offering breathtaking North Alps panoramas (renaming back to Minenohara Kogen). Family friendly with great kids park.

yunomaru.name: Yunomaru Ski Area
yunomaru.summary: Known as the closest powder snow resort to the Tokyo metro area, sitting at 1,700m elevation with high sunny rates and crisp dry powder.

saku-parada.name: Saku Ski Garden Parada
saku-parada.summary: Japan's only expressway PA-connected ski resort, accessible via escalator directly from Sakudaira PA without driving on local roads.

karuizawa-snow-park.name: Karuizawa Snow Park
karuizawa-snow-park.summary: A dedicated family and kids snow park in North Karuizawa featuring large scale snow play areas, gentle beginner slopes, and dog parks.

takamine-mountain-park.name: Takamine Mountain Park
takamine-mountain-park.summary: Formerly Asama 2000 Park. Base elevation of 1,880m and peak at 2,050m. Famous among carving enthusiasts for hard-pack groomed racing quality snow.

yamaboku-wild-snow-park.name: YAMABOKU Wild Snow Park
yamaboku-wild-snow-park.summary: Over 70% of the resort is non-groomed natural powder terrain. Offers snowcat (CAT) skiing tours, making it a true wild powder sanctuary.

hijiri-kogen.name: Hijiri Kogen Ski Resort
hijiri-kogen.summary: A relaxed village-run ski resort at the base of Mt. Hijiri. Free from crowds, offering budget-friendly lift tickets and safe slopes for practice.

nozawa-onsen.name: Nozawa Onsen Snow Resort
nozawa-onsen.summary: Iconic Japanese ski village combining Mt. Kenashi's deep powder, a 10km long run, 2 gondolas, and historic free public hot springs (Sotoyu).

togari-onsen.name: Togari Onsen Ski Resort
togari-onsen.summary: Located across the Chikuma River from Nozawa Onsen. Offers great natural powder, Japan's pioneer snow bike park, and cozy hot spring baths.

romance-no-kamisama.name: Snow Resort Romance no Kamisama
romance-no-kamisama.summary: Formerly Kijimadaira, named after Kohmi Hirose's hit song. Home to Japan's steepest 46-degree slope (Pioneer Course) and wide beginner runs.

sakae-club.name: Sakae Club Ski Area
sakae-club.summary: Tucked away in Sakae Village, one of Japan's snowiest areas. Famous for massive natural snowfall, uncrowded slopes, and authentic local food.

shiga-kogen.name: Shiga Kogen Ski Resort
shiga-kogen.summary: Japan's largest ski area with 18 interconnected resorts under one pass. Features Japan's highest resort summit (Mt. Yokote at 2,307m) and Olympic courses.

ryuo-ski-park.name: Ryuo Ski Park
ryuo-ski-park.summary: Famous for the SORA terrace cloud-sea lounge accessed by a 166-passenger ropeway. Home to the steep 'Kiotoshi' powder course.

x-jam-takaifuji-yomase.name: X-JAM Takaifuji & Yomase Onsen
x-jam-takaifuji-yomase.summary: Fully interconnected ski resort combining X-JAM Takaifuji's premier terrain park (kickers, jibs, halfpipe) with Yomase Onsen's wide carving slopes and famous Tomi-no-yu outdoor hot spring.

komaruyama.name: Komaruyama Ski Resort
komaruyama.summary: Friendly, compact ski resort in Kitashiga with gentle, open slopes ideal for beginners, student groups, and families practicing basic technique.

marunuma-kogen.name: Marunuma Kogen Ski Resort
marunuma-kogen.summary: Features high-altitude powder snow at 2,000m and a long 4km run. Take the Nikko Shirane Ropeway directly to the summit.

minakami-hodaigi.name: Gunma Minakami Hodaigi Ski Resort
minakami-hodaigi.summary: Abundant snowfall and 16 diverse courses ranging from steep unpaved powder runs to gentle beginner slopes in the Minakami area.

ogna-hotaka.name: Ogna Hotaka Ski Resort
ogna-hotaka.summary: Spectacular views from 1,820m elevation and natural powder snow across 13 courses with natural terrain for all skill levels.

hunter-mountain-shiobara.name: Hunter Mountain Shiobara
hunter-mountain-shiobara.summary: One of the largest resorts near Tokyo, featuring 12 varied courses, a gondola, and a full terrain park for families and experts alike.

katashina-kogen.name: Katashina Kogen Ski Resort
katashina-kogen.summary: The only skiers-only resort in Kanto. A safe, family-oriented resort collaborating with Miffy for a peaceful experience.

edelweiss-ski-resort.name: Edelweiss Ski Resort
edelweiss-ski-resort.summary: Located near Nikko Kinugawa Onsen, offering gentle open slopes, a kids' snow park, and a dog run for a relaxed holiday.

snow-park-oze-tokura.name: Snow Park Oze Tokura
snow-park-oze-tokura.summary: Renowned for its high-caliber terrain park, tree runs, and competition-grade courses. A hub for freestylers and racers.

tambara-ski-park.name: Tambara Ski Park
tambara-ski-park.summary: Over 80% beginner and intermediate courses with high-quality silky powder snow and easy car accessibility.

okutone-snow-park.name: Okutone Snow Park
okutone-snow-park.summary: Just 10km from Minakami IC. Features night skiing up to 2.5km long and free lift passes for elementary kids.

norn-minakami.name: Norn Minakami Ski Resort
norn-minakami.summary: Only 3km from Minakami IC — the fastest resort accessible from Tokyo. Late night skiing available until 10pm on Fridays and Saturdays.

minakami-kogen-resort.name: Minakami Kogen Ski Resort
minakami-kogen-resort.summary: Directly connected to Minakami Kogen Hotel 200. Packed with family activities like 2 kids' snow parks and dog sledding.

minakami-fujiwara.name: Minakami Kogen Fujiwara Ski Resort
minakami-fujiwara.summary: Adjacent to Hotel Sunbird with gentle slopes ideal for beginners and sledding, plus hot spring baths after skiing.

white-valley-minakami.name: White Valley Minakami
white-valley-minakami.summary: Famous for its 'Premium Powder Days' where 90% of the slopes are left unpaved for fresh powder lovers.

nikko-yumoto-onsen.name: Nikko Yumoto Onsen Ski Resort
nikko-yumoto-onsen.summary: Adjacent to the hot spring village in Nikko National Park. Features wide, gentle slopes for beginners, families, and relaxing onsen trips.

mt-t-hoshino.name: Mt.T by Hoshino Resorts
mt-t-hoshino.summary: Formerly Tanigawadake Tenjindaira, rebranded as 'Mt.T' by Hoshino Resorts. Famous for its massive snowfall, steep powder bowls, tree runs, and ropeway access to Mt. Tanigawa.
